feature: Select a range of time on the ruler
summary: Drag along the ruler to select a stretch of time across every track, then put a transition on the cuts inside it, cut at its ends, delete it with or without closing the gap, caption it or export it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a recording and press Edit so the timeline is up.

try.do: Drag along the ruler from one moment to another, away from the red playhead.
Drag the green grip at either end of the band to move that end.
Press Cmd-T to put the default transition on every cut inside the range.
Put the playhead inside the range, right-click the ruler and choose Split at Range Edges.
Press Delete: the stretch comes out and the gap stays.
Undo, then press Shift-Delete: the stretch comes out and the gap closes.
Right-click the range and choose Add Captions for Range.
Click the ruler outside the range to let it go.

evaluate: Does dragging the ruler to draw a range feel right, now that scrubbing means grabbing the playhead itself?
Is the band on the ruler plus the wash down the tracks enough to tell a range is selected?
Should Delete and Ripple Delete keep those names, or do you want Premiere's Lift and Extract in the range menu?
Is it right that a click outside a drawn range drops it, while In and Out set with I and O stay?
rough: A drag on the ruler no longer scrubs unless it starts on the playhead; the scrub bar above the tracks and J, K, L still scrub from anywhere.
Merge into One Clip, the marquee over the tracks, Option-drag and R for a track-only range, and Cmd-C/X/V of a range are not here yet. Each is its own task.
The range's actions are on the ruler's right-click only. Right-clicking a clip inside the range still gives the clip's menu.
Add Captions for Range listens to the whole recording and keeps only the lines inside the range, so it takes as long as Add Captions on a long take.
No mock draws a range, so the band follows the existing green In and Out wash on the ruler.
Pictures are from the loop's probe app with Screen Recording granted and the screen unlocked; the hand-drag picture is from the separate walk that uses a real pointer.
